topics.label: Lecture opening and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes students and frames the lecture by stating its subject and learning objectives.

topics.label: Surgery and radiotherapy in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how surgery and radiotherapy treat tumors and how early detection and chemotherapy can support those approaches.

topics.label: Cytotoxic chemotherapy: effects, efficacy and limitations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes how cytotoxic drugs damage cancer cells, their clinical benefits, and the toxicity and resistance that limit their use.

topics.label: Targeting hormone-dependent cancers
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic shows how blocking estrogen or androgen signaling can inhibit cancers that remain dependent on those hormones.

topics.label: Exploiting cancer-cell defects to drive selective killing
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how defects in cell-cycle checkpoints or DNA repair can make cancer cells especially vulnerable to radiation, oncolytic viruses, or PARP inhibition.

topics.label: Oncogene addiction and genome-guided cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how cancer-driving genomic changes can guide the selection of targeted treatments.

topics.label: Kinase inhibitors, resistance and chronic disease management
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how kinase inhibitors block activated kinases and how selectivity problems, resistance, and side effects complicate their long-term use.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies in cancer therapy
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes antibodies that block cancer-associated receptors or recruit immune mechanisms to attack cells expressing their targets.

topics.label: Antibody–drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how an antibody can deliver a cytotoxic drug to cells bearing a selected surface target.

topics.label: Evidence for immune surveillance against cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic assesses the evidence that the immune system naturally helps protect against cancer.

topics.label: Checkpoint inhibition and tumour neoantigens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how checkpoint blockade can reactivate T cells and how tumour mutations may provide antigens for those cells to recognize.

topics.label: T-cell-engaging and CAR T-cell therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe treatments that direct T cells toward tumour cells, either by bringing the cells together with bispecific engagers or by engineering patient T cells.

topics.label: Cancer therapy challenges and personalised treatment
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic synthesizes the challenges of treatment and explains how biomarkers and genomic information may help match patients to therapies.

topics.label: Cancer outcome trends, prevention and early detection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic considers how prevention and early detection have contributed to changing cancer incidence and outcomes.

topics.label: Future cancer care and the dilemma of changing proven treatments
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics consider future directions and ethical choices in cancer care, including whether to test new approaches when established treatments already achieve strong outcomes.
